expectations.text: The already-implemented spec file's original content was NOT modified/rewritten in place
expectations.evidence: Agent confirms v1's title/body (including empty Requirements heading) are byte-identical before/after; only chron spec revise touched v1's frontmatter.

expectations.text: chron spec revise was invoked (not a manual edit of the implemented file, not chron spec new on a fresh capability name)
expectations.evidence: 'chron spec revise oauth-login "OAuth login with Google, GitHub, Apple Sign-In, and refresh token rotation"' was run.

expectations.text: The new version's frontmatter has status: proposed and supersedes pointing at the previous (implemented) version
The new version's requirements are a full self-contained snapshot including Apple Sign-In, not just a diff/delta noting the addition
expectations.evidence: v2's Requirements section restates the full current requirement set (Google/GitHub/Apple login, rotation-on-use, reuse detection, account linking, profile normalization) as standalone bullets, not a pointer back to v1 -- exactly the full-snapshot convention the design calls for. A short 'What changed and why' section explains the delta narratively, separate from the requirements themselves.

expectations.text: The previous version's status became superseded and its superseded_by field points at the new version
expectations.evidence: Handled automatically by chron spec revise per the agent's report (consistent with internal/spec's tested behavior).

notes: This is the clearest with-skill vs baseline differentiator across all three evals: baseline correctly used chron spec revise and avoided hand-editing v1, but wrote a delta-style note pointing back at v1 rather than a full snapshot. The skill's explicit 'never a diff against the previous version' instruction is what produced the correct behavior here.
